verdict: Lead volume and efficiency both dropped this week; Google spend is being addressed.
narrative: Over the last 28 days you received 133 leads at an average cost of $16.49 per lead, but the most recent 7 days showed a 35% drop in lead volume alongside a 30% rise in cost per lead — efficiency and volume deteriorating at the same time. The primary driver is Meta, which is carrying all 133 leads on its own while ad efficiency has softened. Google Ads spent $501 over the full 28-day window and produced zero conversions, making it a non-contributing channel; that budget is being reallocated. Separately, your pipeline shows 154 new opportunities created in the period but zero appointments and zero closed — leads are reaching the CRM, but something in the intake process is not converting them, and that is being investigated now. New ad creative, paid landing pages, and audience improvements are in motion and are expected to stabilise cost per lead heading into the next period.

highlights.phrase: leads received in the last 28 days, all from Meta
spent on Google Ads this period with zero leads to show for it
new opportunities in your pipeline, with none yet converted to appointments

watch_item.issue: Cost per lead rose 30% week-over-week while lead volume fell 35%, and Google Ads produced no results on $501 in spend.
watch_item.fix: Google spend is being paused and redirected to Meta; creative is being refreshed this week to arrest the efficiency slide.
